reading.body:
CyberNAP Glen Burnie occupies 15 acres and roughly 300,000 square feet in a converted department store north of Fort Meade, Maryland, on Ritchie Highway. The operator has not published the facility's IT capacity in megawatts, so its power allocation to AI workloads cannot be assessed from public data.

Maryland has 11 mapped data center facilities, of which only 3 have published power figures totaling 9.3 megawatts. This campus ranks fourth among published capacities in the state, meaning at least one facility has disclosed more capacity than CyberNAP Glen Burnie, yet this campus still lacks a published figure, so that ranking reflects incomplete information.

Without published power consumption, the scale of this facility relative to AI infrastructure deployment cannot be determined. The building's origin as a converted retail structure and its suburban location near a federal facility constrain its relevance to the grid-as-binding-constraint question unless the operator discloses actual IT load.
